title: The rest of the Honolulu sextet and writing an arrangement a day
summary: He names the piano player and drummer, and says he wrote a new arrangement every day.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: That's what I've heard. After Francis King, who else was in the band?
Okay, we'll get back to it. [PAUL CHANG]
Yes, we'll have to come back to that. Make a note, and we'll come back to that.

My piano player was Bernie (or Bernard) Concepcion, of Filipino extraction. These were all very good musicians, incidentally. And my drummer was Pepe Bowman. We called him Pappy. They used to all call me "Pops." I don't know why, because we were all the same age, but I guess by my
having more experience than these guys, they just called me Pops -- and it was all right.
But I had fun. I used to make a point of doing one arrangement, at least one arrangement every day, so we'd have fresh things to play -- and we built up quite a repertoire.
